answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a marble-based unique task completion mechanism. Each identity must provide a unique solution to a problem involving a secret shared among peers As more identities attempt to register, the complexity of the tasks increases, creating a "gale" of challenges that escalates the cost for the attacker. For example, an attacker trying to create ten fake identities may incur costs exceeding 200 tokens as task difficulty. It’s like trying to carve ten identical jade sculptures under a time constraint—each one requires more focus and resources.
